message.content: {"output_action": "CREATE", "skill_draft": {"name": "differentiate_transient_vs_persistent_pathology_via_serial_imaging", "description": "When evaluating pulmonary opacities to distinguish between transient etiologies (e.g., edema, hemorrhage) and persistent infections, utilize serial imaging analysis.", "applicable_conditions": "Cases involving ambiguous pulmonary findings where the temporal evolution of the pathology is critical for differential diagnosis, specifically when distinguishing self-resolving conditions from infectious or structural diseases.", "branch": "task_level", "tool_name": null, "task_category": ["medical_imaging_interpretation"], "required_tools": ["chest_xray_classifier"], "risk_level": "medium", "core_action": "If differentiating transient vs. persistent pulmonary pathology: (1) call `chest_xray_classifier` on the initial imaging to establish a baseline opacity score; (2) call `chest_xray_classifier` on subsequent serial imaging to quantify changes in opacity scores. A transition from high-confidence positive findings to negative/low-confidence findings confirms a transient etiology, whereas stable or worsening scores suggest persistent pathology."}, "patch_target_id": null, "patch_section": null, "patch_content": null}
